notes: Activates the TRD-approved Hermes reasoning-runtime boundary while preserving DirectModelRuntime as a viable fallback.
Groq and OpenRouter credentials remain inside the Hermes service boundary and are never exposed to agents, domain state, browser code or committed configuration.
Hermes is constrained to zero tools, no persistent memory/context, no project-plugin/profile inheritance, no persistent Hermes prompt logs and a Kairo-authenticated versioned invocation contract.
Normal routing is Groq primary with OpenRouter fallback; OpenRouter fallback requires ZDR/no-collection/parameter support and controlled benchmark mode is primary-only.
Python CI uses fake providers for contract tests plus a real pinned Hermes container/version/zero-tool check; it receives no provider credentials and performs no model inference.
No database migration, release, deployment, provider-secret entry, VS-23 live activation or VS-24 promotion is authorized by this slice.

approvals.rationale: The owner explicitly selected Hermes with Groq and OpenRouter, created both provider keys privately, and instructed Go after the bounded Hermes integration direction and secret boundary were explained.

The approved TRD already defines Hermes as the preferred AgentRuntimePort implementation, DirectModelRuntime fallback, provider-neutral model access, secret isolation, zero agent publishing authority and auditable model cost. This slice does not broaden those policies.

The owner's Go instruction authorizes bounded implementation of the agreed Hermes runtime integration. Merge, release, deployment, provider-secret entry and production enablement remain separate approvals.

Implementation and internal review are complete. Exact-head Product Intake, Security and full CI including the installed pinned-Hermes zero-tool container gate must pass before human exact-SHA certification approval is requested.

evidence: RED TypeScript and Python service contracts were committed before corresponding runtime behavior.

A first full CI attempt exposed a strict TypeScript implicit-any defect in the new API validator map while Python Hermes contracts, PostgreSQL migration verification, dependency audit and preflight had passed; the typing defect was repaired without weakening a gate.

Subsequent review added exact pinned Hermes container/version/zero-tool verification, OpenRouter ZDR/no-collection routing, Groq ZDR deployment precondition, Hermes persistent-file-log suppression, provider timeout propagation and forced ambient Hermes profile isolation.
